text.title: Google Analytics 4 Setup Core Rules
text.summary: 9 testable rules every Google Analytics 4 Setup application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: The config MUST record the numeric property id and every data stream's measurement id (`G-` prefix) as separate fields. The `gtag` snippet and Measurement Protocol use the measurement id; the Data API, Admin API and BigQuery dataset name use the numeric property id. Using one where the other is expected is a config error.

rationale.source: Google Analytics Data API documentation; GA4 Measurement Protocol reference

rule.rationale: The ids look interchangeable and are not: a Data API call with `properties/G-XXXX` returns a permission error that reads like a credentials problem and costs an afternoon, and a Measurement Protocol hit with the numeric id is accepted with HTTP 204 and silently discarded.

rule.statement: The config MUST list the state of each enhanced measurement toggle (page views, scrolls, outbound clicks, site search, video engagement, file downloads, form interactions). On single-page applications, either the browser-history page view option is on or the app sends `page_view` manually with `send_page_view: false` in the config call; never both.

rationale.source: Google Analytics Help, 'Enhanced event measurement'; gtag.js reference, send_page_view

rule.rationale: Enhanced measurement is on by default, so an SPA that also pushes its own `page_view` on route change reports two page views per screen and halves every per-page engagement metric. Form interactions and site search fire on parameters the team never chose; undeclared toggles are the usual source of "where did this event come from" tickets.

rule.statement: Every custom event parameter or user property that any report will read MUST be registered as a custom dimension or metric with the correct scope (event, user, item) before the first event that carries it is sent. Standard properties allow 50 event-scoped and 25 user-scoped custom dimensions and 50 custom metrics; check the current limit for your plan before registering, and record the used count in the config.

rationale.source: Google Analytics Help, 'Custom dimensions and metrics'

rule.rationale: Custom dimensions populate only from the date of registration; a parameter sent for three months before anyone registered it is unreportable for those three months, and the BigQuery export is the only place it survives. Teams that register one dimension per experiment hit the 50 cap within a year and cannot delete without losing the report history that referenced the slot.

rule.statement: Conversions MUST be declared as key events by exact event name in the config, and only events present in the property's event list MAY be marked. Standard properties allow 30 key events; check the current limit for your plan. Each key event MUST state its counting method (once per event or once per session).
rule.rationale: Marking `Purchase` as a key event when the site sends `purchase` creates a conversion that never fires, and the mismatch is invisible because the mark saves without error. The counting method decides whether a user who submits a form twice is one lead or two, which is the first number sales will dispute.

rule.statement: Every `purchase` event MUST carry `transaction_id`, `value`, `currency` and an `items` array using the recommended item parameters. The `transaction_id` MUST be the order identifier, unique per order and stable across retries, browser and server sends.

rationale.source: GA4 recommended events reference, purchase; Google Analytics Help, 'Set up ecommerce measurement'

rule.rationale: GA4 deduplicates purchases that share a `transaction_id`, which is the only defence against the user who reloads the confirmation page or the server that retries a Measurement Protocol hit. Without it revenue in GA4 runs ahead of the order table and every ROAS figure downstream inherits the error.

rule.statement: Where users from consent jurisdictions are in scope, the snippet MUST push `gtag('consent', 'default', ...)` with `ad_storage`, `analytics_storage`, `ad_user_data` and `ad_personalization` before the `gtag('config', ...)` call, scoped with `region` where defaults differ, and the consent management platform MUST send `gtag('consent', 'update', ...)` on user choice. The config MUST record the consent mode implementation (basic or advanced).

rationale.source: Google, Consent Mode v2 documentation; Google Ads Help, EU user consent policy

rule.rationale: Defaults pushed after `config` arrive after the first hit has already set cookies, so the implementation is non-compliant while appearing complete. Since March 2024 Google requires the two v2 signals to build EEA audiences and measure conversions in Google Ads; a property without them loses that data without any warning in GA4 itself.

rule.statement: The BigQuery export MUST be linked before the property receives production traffic, with the daily export enabled and the dataset location recorded in the config. Event data retention MUST be set to 14 months (the maximum for standard properties). Any report used for a business decision that would exceed the sampling threshold in explorations (10 million events per query for standard properties; check the current limit for your plan) MUST be built from BigQuery, not from a sampled exploration.

rationale.source: Google Analytics Help, 'BigQuery Export'; Google Analytics Help, 'Data retention'; Google Analytics Help, 'About data sampling'

rule.rationale: The export does not backfill: linking it in month six means the first six months exist only inside GA4's interface. Retention defaults to 2 months, after which explorations quietly stop returning older users. Sampled explorations disagree with themselves run to run, and a decision made on a sampled cohort cannot be reproduced the next day.

rule.statement: Server-side events sent through the Measurement Protocol MUST reuse the `client_id` read from the browser's `_ga` cookie and include the current `session_id` and `engagement_time_msec`; generating a fresh `client_id` server-side is forbidden. The Measurement Protocol `api_secret` MUST be stored server-side only and never shipped to the browser.
rule.rationale: A fresh id per hit turns every server event into a new user with no session, so server-side purchases attribute to `(direct)` and the new-user count doubles. The `api_secret` in client code lets anyone inject events into the property; the standard first sign is a spike of fake purchases from a single country.

rule.statement: The config MUST define the internal-traffic filter (IP rules, and the filter set to active, not testing), the unwanted-referral list covering every payment and authentication domain the checkout passes through (for example the payment provider and the SSO provider), and the cross-domain measurement list when the journey spans more than one domain.

rationale.source: Google Analytics Help, 'Filter out internal traffic'; Google Analytics Help, 'Identify unwanted referrals'; Google Analytics Help, 'Set up cross-domain measurement'

rule.rationale: Without the referral exclusion every purchase that returns from the payment provider starts a new session attributed to `paypal.com / referral`, and the paid campaign that actually drove it gets zero credit. The internal filter defaults to testing mode, which does nothing until someone flips it; office traffic then inflates engagement on every internal tool page.
